description: M4 creates the first real windows, so this file grows for the first time since M2. It grows by two permissions, both on the core event bus, and by nothing else. It did not grow again when the status-window reshape made the status window a control surface and let it edit the watched list, which is the point worth reading here: the four commands that pass grew are Rust functions, taking a word (engine_action), an index (open_watched, which also takes the path that row was showing, and that string can only make the answer a refusal) and a string the page was handed and this process never touches (add_watched_folder, remove_watched_folder). A page that can pause the engine and change what is watched still holds no permission it did not hold before, because none of the four is a plugin command. Everything privileged in this app is still a Rust function reached through the fourteen commands in src/ipc.rs: the core is spawned with std::process::Command, the setup sidecar by src/setup_host.rs, the Run value by src/autostart.rs, the toasts by src/toasts.rs, the folder dialog by ipc::pick_folder, the two folder edits by running the core's own folders subcommand, and Open log and one watched folder by the supervisor thread. NOT granted, deliberately, and each absence is the law it enforces: no dialog:* (the plugin is compiled in for pick_folder and is unreachable from a page), no notification:* (only toasts.rs raises one, off a core event), no opener:* (open_path takes a kind and never a path, so a page cannot name a file), no fs:* (tauri-plugin-fs IS compiled in as of M4, transitively under tauri-plugin-dialog, so the guarantee is the ungranted permission rather than the absent crate: no fs: permission is granted to any webview, and a page therefore has no file system), no shell:* (tauri-plugin-shell is not a dependency either, so there is no path from a webview to a spawn), no core:webview:allow-create-webview-window (window creation is the closed two-page enum in src/windows.rs, which is where the OAuth law stops being a convention and becomes a build setting), and as of M5 no updater:* either. tauri-plugin-updater is compiled in and ships four commands, check, download, install and downloadAndInstall, and a page is granted none of them. That absence is the loudest one in this file: install replaces this running process with an installer, so a page that could reach it could restart the machine's uploader whenever it liked and could do it in the middle of a batch, which is the one thing TRAY-DESIGN section 5's update policy exists to forbid. The whole policy lives in src/updater.rs and its only call site is the quit path in src/supervisor.rs, so the update story grew no IPC at all: the fourteen commands are still fourteen. The two windows named below are the only ones this app can build.

permissions.$reason: The setup window subscribes to the setup-event channel, which is how the wizard's NDJSON stream reaches the page. Without it the first-run window renders once and never hears another word: the whole walk is events. It grants listening only. Emitting stays ungranted, so a page cannot forge an event another part of this app would act on.

The other half of the same subscription. A window destroyed on close has to be able to let go of its listener, and a listener that outlives its window is exactly the leak the create-on-demand design exists to avoid.
